# Was the Samsung Ads data breach a hack?

**Confirmed.** A vendor incident, yes: Samsung says a third-party vendor that handled Samsung Ads North America advertising data was involved. Whether Samsung's own systems were hacked is not established.

Incident: Samsung Ads North America vendor breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Samsung smart TV data leak and the Samsung Ads vendor breach. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 12:25 PM ET.

Picture: Samsung smart TVs on display in a shop. Image: Raysonho, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SamsungSmartTV.JPG).

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Samsung, Cybernews, Android Headlines, DailySecu or any other company, news outlet, government agency, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 12:25 PM ET: **Samsung says a third-party vendor for Samsung Ads North America was involved; a ransomware group says it posted 220MB.** First build from Cybernews and DailySecu (both Tier 2, read Nov 22; Samsung gave each its statement) and Android Headlines (relays Cybernews). c001 vendor incident Confirmed on Samsung's own statement to two independent outlets; no Samsung page was found. c002 to c005 and c008 Reported (group claim and file contents as described by Cybernews; the group's post was not visited). c006 hack of Samsung's own systems and c007 vendor and method Not established. Privacy check done: no employees, officials or contacts named; employee details in the files are not repeated.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. About 220MB posted, per Cybernews: roughly 150,000 TV viewing events, 42,600 political ad records and 99,100 AI training records. Samsung has not said how much was affected.
- Who is affected: Not yet clear. The dump is said to hold smart TV viewing events with city and ZIP code, and political ad records, from Samsung's North America advertising business. Samsung says scope is still being worked out with the vendor.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 220MB | Posted by n0n | Per Cybernews |
| 150K | TV viewing events | 2024; no titles; per Cybernews |
| 42.6K | Political ad records | Sept to Oct 2026; per Cybernews |

### Known so far

- Samsung says a third-party vendor for Samsung Ads North America was involved.
- Samsung says the vendor's early findings show some Samsung information may have been affected.

### Not known yet

- What data was really taken; the contents come from Cybernews, not Samsung.
- Which vendor, and how the attacker got in.
- Whether Samsung's own systems were accessed.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the time of this report on Nov 22, 2026.

- A Samsung newsroom page or notice with the statement. It appears only as quotes to Cybernews and DailySecu.
- The name of the vendor, or how the attacker got in.
- A statement on whether Samsung's own systems were accessed.
- Samsung confirming what data was in the dump, or how many people it covers.
- Any regulator notice or customer notice from Samsung.
- Any attribution beyond the group's own claim as reported by Cybernews.

We did not visit the group's leak page.
